notes: Four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security) via background subagents covering 2026-10-14/15. Routine EGRESS_BLOCKED/DNS-failure on nearly every org-domain WebFetch; all four lanes worked around it via WebSearch. The calendar is now dense (646 entries going in) so most candidates each lane surfaced were already on file at equal or better confidence -- this was a correction-heavy run: two same-day Anthropic announcements (election safeguards, independent-evaluator program) filed fresh; six genuinely new cloud/devtools EOL entries (Azure AI Anomaly Detector/Personalizer, Google Cloud Run Node.js 20, AWS Proton, Amazon Lookout for Equipment, Amazon Pinpoint) turned out to already be on file except Lookout for Equipment, which was new; three new CISA KEV federal remediation deadlines (Ivanti Connect Secure, a Palo Alto/Cisco/Ahsay batch, Atlassian Data Center) resolve open questions from the last few runs about whether those CVEs had landed in the catalog yet; and three existing entries got real corrections -- TSMC's Q3 2026 earnings entry now carries the actual reported results instead of pre-earnings guidance, Meta's and Microsoft's Q1/Q3 earnings dates moved from tracker-estimate 'expected' placeholders to each company's own confirmed date, and Python 3.15.0's release date corrected from PEP 790's original Oct 1 target to the actual Oct 9 GA (an extra release candidate was needed). ASML's Q3 earnings, NVIDIA GTC 2027, the FTC v. Amazon trial date, Apple's EU App Store terms, and the Google Play API-level-36 deadline were all re-found by lanes but already on file with equal or better sourcing, so left untouched. The Flax Typhoon five-CVE KEV deadline (already filed at 'expected') was independently re-confirmed by the security lane with the same exact CVE list from a second source, but no new primary CISA link was found so it was not touched.
concerns: data/events/2026-10.json carries two near-duplicate Python 3.15.0 entries ('python-software-foundation-python-3-15-0-final-release-2026-10' and 'python-software-foundation-python-3-15-0-general-availabilit-2026-10'), both originally dated 2026-10-01 from PEP 790's schedule. This run corrected one of them to the real Oct 9 GA date using python.org's own release page; the other was deliberately left untouched rather than compounding the duplicate. A maintainer should merge the pair.

data/events/2026-10.json also carries two near-duplicate Azure AI retirement entries ('microsoft-azure-azure-retires-anomaly-detector-metrics-advis-2026-10' and 'microsoft-azure-azure-retires-personalizer-anomaly-detector-2026-10'), both dated 2026-10-01 for the same three Azure AI services (Anomaly Detector, Metrics Advisor, Personalizer). This run's devtools/cloud lane re-found the same fact and deliberately did not file a third copy. A maintainer should merge these two.

The devtools/cloud lane found conflicting official AWS dates for AWS IoT Greengrass V1's end of support: AWS's own sunset-services table gives 2026-10-01, while Greengrass V1's own maintenance-policy doc gives 2026-10-07. Not filed per the no-guessing-dates rule; a maintainer with reliable fetch access to docs.aws.amazon.com should reconcile which is current.

Microsoft's fiscal Q1 2027 earnings date correction (Oct 27 -> Oct 28) in this run's findings relies on Finviz quoting a Microsoft press release, not a direct read of Microsoft's own investor-relations page (unreachable via WebFetch this run). Filed at 'confirmed' since the source does quote Microsoft's own announcement, but worth a maintainer's direct double-check against microsoft.com/en-us/investor once fetch access works.

AWS WAF Classic's retirement date could not be confirmed on any AWS page this run (AWS points to the per-account Health Dashboard instead of a public date) -- left out entirely rather than guessed; a maintainer with account-level AWS access could pin this down.

Azure OpenAI's reported gpt-4o/gpt-4o-mini retirement (Oct 1, 2026 per third-party trackers) was deliberately excluded from the devtools/cloud lane as an AI-model lifecycle fact rather than pure cloud-service infrastructure -- if it isn't already on file as an 'ai' entry from a prior run, it's worth a dedicated check.
